independence: written from the r3 text (PREREG sections 1.1 to 6.3, 4, 5.3) and the ROOT_ITEMS M-12 case list; it does not read or import the text stage's verify_r3_rules_c4.py or R3_RULES_SELFTEST.json
model: synthetic rows only (dimensionless ratios). Row kinds: HIT (|r| <= 1), MISS (|r| > 1, signed), NULL (a VALID row with a null ratio: a MISS with no sign, counted in U, with a frozen prediction), LATE (a LATE-gate row: counted as a MISS with no ratio, in U, no frozen prediction), INVALID. The first TRANSITION row plays Q25, the one TSR-flagged row. STAGE0 is NOT_EVALUATED_BEFORE_FREEZE unless a case sets it.

text_findings.claim: R-DRIFT part 1 is not uniquely defined when DT-S0G reads AGAINST and OUTER_FAILURE does not hold. Section 3 says "INCONSISTENT when any registered against-condition of the reading holds. Against takes precedence"; the closed mapping of section 6.3 says "Part 1 is shown for an outcome where OUTER_FAILURE holds; otherwise part 1 is NOT_ADDRESSED (PATTERN_NOT_HELD)". The two read INCONSISTENT and NOT_ADDRESSED (PATTERN_NOT_HELD) on the same outcome.
text_findings.reproduction: PATTERN_SUITE_RESULTS.json drift_conflict_case: PRIMARY OUTER 8 HIT at r = 0.2; STAGE0 twin 8 HIT at r = 0.5; every other row HIT, Q01/Q02 INVALID; DT-S0G AGAINST {'n': 8, 'H_P': 8, 'H_S': 8, 'A_P': 0.2, 'A_S': 0.5}
text_findings.fix: state which rule governs R-DRIFT part 1 without OUTER_FAILURE (for example: "the 6.3 mapping governs R-DRIFT; without OUTER_FAILURE part 1 is NOT_ADDRESSED (PATTERN_NOT_HELD) whatever DT-S0G reads"), and add the case to M-12

text_findings.claim: CROSSING can hold while OUTER is not miss-dominated (so P11 is false). The section 2 table attaches P11g to P11 ("flag P11g if CROSSING"); section 4 lists P11g as a pattern of its own, and R-HIST says "P1g or P11g makes it more specific". This suite reads P11g = P11 and CROSSING; the reading P11g = CROSSING differs on 788 of the random registered-size classifications. P1g has no such gap: GROWING implies P1 (0 exceptions).

text_findings.fix: write "P11g: P11 holds and CROSSING holds" in the table, or say that P11g is reported only with P11

text_findings.claim: A reading can read CONSISTENT although no MISS row in its scope can be cited: when every MISS row of the triggering zone is a LATE-gate row (no frozen prediction). It happens for the OUTER readings (U1L, the M-15 all-LATE OUTER zone), for the INNER readings under P15 (L2: 12 LATE rows and 10 HIT rows), under P7 (L4) and, in the enumeration, under P13. C-9 consequence (iv) and M-15 record only the all-LATE OUTER zone. Readings affected in the exhaustive LATE enumeration: ['R-DRIFT', 'R-GEFF', 'R-GEO', 'R-HIST', 'R-MF', 'R-ML', 'R-NAX', 'R-SPEC'].
text_findings.reproduction: named cases U1L_all_late_outer, L2, L4 (readings with scope_has_citable_miss false); exhaustive_late_6state_1to3 late_version_metrics
text_findings.fix: extend C-9 (iv) and M-15 to the general case, or state that such a reading is reported with "no citable MISS row"

text_findings.claim: When both STAGE0 conditions fail, 6.3 and M-14 do not say whether one reason or both are printed ("with the reason RECEIPTS_AFTER_STEP4 if (a) fails, or NO_SEALED_SUCCESSOR if (b) fails"). This suite prints both.

Under NOT_READ, "each output whose own input is defective reads NOT_AVAILABLE" needs a map from each stop code to the outputs it touches; the text does not give one. This suite assumes STOP_AFFECTS (for example a sensitivity field defect touches only the sensitivity column, a TSR flag-table stop only P10, R-TSR and the flag column, and a reference-member or zone-table stop every output, the E3 line included). Two M-12 implementations could differ here.
text_findings.reproduction: other_rule_cases NR_field_defect, NR_E3_input_defective, NR_tsr_only; suite STOP_AFFECTS
